name: Manifested
body:
Sometimes the souls of the departed do not pass gently into the afterlife that awaits them. Powerful emotions swirl around these spirits, causing them to cling to existence, becoming the ghost-like outsiders known as phantoms. In most cases, these phantoms cannot manifest in the Material Plane without the aid of a powerful psychic ally known as a spiritualist. However, in some extremely rare cases, these phantoms have been known to fully manifest on their own—a powerful burst of magic, emotion, and circumstance allowing them to turn the swirling ectoplasm of the Ethereal into a fully-realized material body.

Physical

In many ways, the manifested look just like the ordinary mortal humanoids they were before they passed away. Unlike a ghost, their bodies are fully material, even though the matter they are formed from may not behave in completely mundane ways.

Upon closer inspection, a manifested’s appearance usually contains some hints as to their true, otherworldly nature. Their outline may blur slightly when they move, their eyes may glow with an eerie green light when they feel strong emotion, or a distant creaking sound may be heard whenever they speak.

Manifested may reappear in the Material Plane soon after their death or generations later. They usually manifest at an idealized age, and dress according to how they dressed at that age. Because of their strong emotional ties to their own self-image, a manifested usually has difficulty adapting to new styles of fashion.

A manifested does not age, and does not die of old age. Like a phantom, they may eventually cross over into the true afterlife once they achieve the objective that created their emotional focus in the first place, or by finding the solace and emotional balance that had previously eluded them.

Social

Just like a phantom, a manifested can only be created through strong emotion. While they may not always retain all of the memories of their previous life, that emotional imprint is indelible and is the driving force behind everything the manifested does.

Manifested “wear their hearts on their sleeves,” so to speak. While they are as diverse as just about any other people, they are usually not very introverted when it comes to displaying their emotions. Some have a harder time than others forming bonds with mortals, but all have a deep need to achieve something left undone during their original lifespan, and that desire usually leads to interaction with others, exploration, and adventure—and sometimes even to personal growth.

Alignment And Religion

Manifested can be of any alignment. Their alignment often reflects the outlook they had in life, although the new perspective they have as a manifested, and the intense emotional impulses that drive them, may persuade them more than any fleeting memories of their past life. If anything, these emotions often cause manifested to drift toward more Chaotic tendencies, as they place more of a priority on the gut instincts of their feelings, and less on conformity and tradition.

Religion is a secondary concern, at best, for many manifested. Some continue the faiths that they practiced in life, but many feel betrayed by the cycle of life and death, abandoned by the gods who were supposed to welcome them to the afterlife. Many tend to focus on their own, very personal needs and philosophies, perhaps driven by the all-consuming emotional foci that now fuel their very existences. There are some, however, that do go seeking for greater meaning—wondering what truths may have eluded them and led to this indeterminate state that has left them haunting the world rather than truly living in it.

Names

Most manifested retain the names that they used in life, although some have trouble recalling these and take new names or nicknames. A few examples of the new names that a manifested may take include the following (choose or roll 1d20): 1 Banquo, 2 Barbs, 3 Berry, 4 Buzz, 5 Crow, 6 Elvira, 7 Friendly, 8 Hetty, 9 Kat, 10 Maddie, 11 Marl, 12 Mona, 13 Moon, 14 Nick, 15 Pinky, 16 Robin, 17 Sammy, 18 Sue, 19 Thelma, 20 Vigo

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are preternaturally agile and bold, but you lack many of the memories and logical connections you had formed in life. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Cha, –2 Int [standard]. (0)
Size At character creation, choose either Medium or Small size, reflecting the size you were as a mortal. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks; you must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Medium or Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet, and your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are an Outsider with the phantom subtype. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any language except for secret languages. (1)
Alternate Species Traits
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Incorporeal Step (Ex)

Once per day, when you move more than 5 feet, you can become incorporeal until you stop moving. During this time, you gain all of the traits of the incorporeal universal monster ability (see Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Bestiary, page 301). You lose any natural armor bonus you possess, but gain a deflection bonus to AC equal to your Charisma bonus. (2)

Overly Emotional You suffer a –2 penalty on all saving throws against spells and effects with the emotion descriptor. (–1)
Slam You can make a slam attack with either or both arms as long as you do not use them to make weapon or claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage (or 1d3 if you are size Small). (2)
Emotional Focus Like a phantom, every manifested has an emotional focus—a powerful emotion based on some experience from their past life, which keeps them tethered to their new existence as a manifested. Your emotional focus grants you a +2 species bonus in two different skills, and also grants you a spell-like ability that you can use once per day. Your character level is your caster level for this spell-like ability, and Charisma is your casting ability. (4)
Anger: Intimidate, Survival; wrath
Dedication: Diplomacy, Sense Motive; shield other
Despair: Intimidate, Stealth; qualm
Desperation: Acrobatics, Escape Artist; aspect of the bear
Fear: Intimidate, Stealth; paranoia
Greed: Appraise, Sleight of Hand; demand offering
Hatred: Acrobatics, Perception; bloodbath
Jealousy: Appraise, Bluff; compel hostility
Kindness: Diplomacy, Heal; euphoric cloud
Lust: Bluff, Diplomacy; unnatural lust
Pride: Intimidate, Perception; shamefully overdressed
Remorse: Perception, Sense Motive; miserable pity
Suffering: Climb, Heal; mindshock
Whimsy: Acrobatics, Perception; absurdity
Zeal: Acrobatics, Survival; false life
Total: 11 RP (advanced)
Feats
Emotionally-Charged Slams

As a creature of unbridled emotional energy, there are times when you like to use your fists to solve your problems.

Prerequisite(s): manifested, slam attack, emotional focus species trait.

Benefit(s): You gain a special ability that applies to your slam attacks, depending upon your emotional focus, as follows:

Anger: Your slam attacks deal damage as if you were one size category larger than your actual size. For example, if you are size Medium, your slam attacks deal damage as if were a Large creature (1d6 + your Strength modifier) instead of their normal damage. This increase stacks with the Improved Natural Attack feat and any other effects that may increase your slam’s damage die.
Dedication: When you hit a creature with your slam attack, you gain a +2 bonus to your AC against that creature for 1 round. If you hit the same creature multiple times, this bonus stacks.
Despair: A creature hit by your slam attack must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Charisma modifier) or take a –2 penalty on attack rolls and damage rolls for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting emotion effect; the penalty does not stack.
Desperation: You can add your Dexterity modifier to attack and damage rolls with your slam attacks instead of your Strength modifier.
Fear: A creature hit by your slam attack must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Charisma modifier) or become shaken for 1d4 rounds. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. If the creature is already shaken, the condition does not worsen, but the duration is extended.
Greed: When you use a slam attack to score a critical hit against a significant opponent, or reduce a significant opponent to 0 hit points, you gain 2d4 temporary hit points. These temporary hit points stack, and last for a maximum of 1 hour.
Hatred: You gain a +1 bonus on attack rolls and damage rolls with your slam attacks against the creature that most recently harmed you.
Jealousy: You gain sneak attack +1d6 when using your slam attack, as the rogue class feature.
Kindness: When you hit a creature with your slam attack, you can designate one ally that you can see or sense. That ally gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls against that same creature for 1 round. If you hit the same creature multiple times, this bonus stacks.
Lust: You can choose to have your slam deal nonlethal damage. If you do so, a creature struck by the slam attack must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Charisma modifier) or become staggered for 1 round. If the creature is already staggered, the condition does not worsen, but the duration is extended.
Pride: When you hit a creature with your slam attack, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls against that creature for 1 round, but you take a –2 penalty to your AC against that creature for the same duration. If you hit the same creature multiple times, the bonus and penalty both stack.
Remorse: When you hit a creature with your slam attack, that creature must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Charisma modifier) or any attacks targeting the creature gain a +1 bonus on their attack rolls and damage rolls until the beginning of your next turn. Penalties from multiple hits don’t stack.
Suffering: When you hit a creature with your slam attack, you also deal 1 point of bleed damage. If you hit the same creature multiple times, this bleed damage stacks.
Whimsy: When you confirm a critical hit against a significant opponent, you gain a free trip attack against that opponent. You can choose to use your Charisma modifier in place of your Strength modifier to determine your CMB for this trip attack, and your attempt does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
Zeal: Your slam attack has a critical threat range of 19–20 and a critical multiplier of ×3.
Extra Incorporeal Step

You can turn incorporeal more frequently.

Prerequisite(s): manifested, incorporeal step species trait.

Benefit(s): You can use your incorporeal step trait one a time each day.

Special: You can take this feat multiple times. Each time, you gain one additional use of this ability per day.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +10 minutes to the duration of your mutagens.
Arcanist Gain +1/6 of a new arcanist exploit.
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Bloodrager Add +1/4 to your effective bloodrager class level when determining the strength of your bloodrager bloodline powers.
Brawler Add +1/4 to your effective brawler level to determine your unarmed strike damage.
Cavalier Add +1/4 to your banner bonus.
Fighter Gain a +1 bonus to your CMD when resisting bull rush and grapple attempts.
Kineticist Gain +1/5 of the Extra Wild Talent feat. This feat must be spent on an aether-element talent.
Medium When gaining a taboo, you can use spirit surge without incurring influence an additional +1/4 time per day.
Mesmerist Increase your bonus damage from painful stare by +1/2 point.
Occultist Increase the resistance bonus on saving throws from your warding talisman resonant power by +1/5.
Oracle Add +1/4 to your caster level when casting spells with the emotion descriptor.
Psychic Treat your Charisma bonus as +1/3 point higher for the purpose of determining the number of uses or rounds per day of your discipline powers.
Ranger Add +1/4 to a single existing favored enemy bonus (maximum bonus +1 per favored enemy).
Rogue Gain +1/4 additional use of your incorporeal step species trait per day.
Shaman Add +1 spell from the psychic spell list that isn’t on the shaman spell list to your shaman spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Add +1/4 to your caster level when casting spells with the emotion descriptor.
Spiritualist Treat your effective spiritualist level as +1/4 higher for the purpose of determining how many uses you gain each day of each spell-like ability granted by the emotional power class feature. You must have the fractured mind archetype to select this benefit.
Summoner Add +1/4 to your shield ally bonus (maximum +2).
Swashbuckler Increase the total number of points in your panache pool by +1/4.
Vigilante Add +1/2 to the DC increase from unshakable.
Witch Add +1 spell from the witch spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
